bounds: A valuation cap and a discount are two different ways a SAFE can set a conversion price, if its terms include them.
A cap uses a stated company valuation and a capitalization definition; a discount reduces the next financing’s share price by a percentage.
In a simplified example, assume a $500 SAFE, an $8 million cap, a $20 million priced round, and ten million fully diluted pre-conversion shares.
The cap calculation gives $0.80 per share, while the round price is $2.00, so the cap-based illustration gives 625 shares versus 250 at the round price.
That is not a guaranteed ownership percentage.
It ignores new money, other instruments, option-pool changes, and contract-specific details.
If a SAFE also has a 20% discount to a $2 round price, the discounted price would be $1.60.
Which term governs depends on the actual agreement.
Check the capitalization definition and conversion formula carefully.
